task: Write one sentence of your own using the word loquacious. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know loquacious should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Our loquacious cousin can spin twenty easy minutes of talk out of a walk to the mailbox, and somehow you listen.
Conversational is the base rung, far below loquacious — it just means able to hold up an ordinary exchange.
Talkative comes closer but stops short of loquacious — a talkative friend talks a lot, while a loquacious one talks in tumbling, unbroken abundance.

Chatty is light, sociable talk — friendly small exchanges over a fence or between errands. Loquacious describes real volume: talk in easy, tumbling abundance, an hour where a sentence would do. A chatty neighbor passes the time of day; a loquacious one narrates the whole afternoon.

Wordy faults the writing, not the writer: more words on the page than the idea needs, the kind an editor trims. Loquacious describes a person's abundant flow of talk, and it passes no judgment — a loquacious host can be a delight. Reports are wordy; people are loquacious.
